citation: George Glessner, photograph of an Illinois Central train at the foot of 18th Street, c. 1888, looking east from the end of the street. Reproduced in "The early history of Prairie Avenue", Glessner House blog, June 2020.
author: George Glessner
repository: Glessner House (the museum's collection, as reproduced on its blog)
locator: The blog's 'Illinois Central tracks' image; the project's copy is kevinrhaas/chicago-images prairie-1904/files/a18-gh-ic-train-foot-of-18th-c1888.jpg (record a18-gh-ic-train-foot-of-18th-c1888).
rights_note: Permission requested from Glessner House Museum, 2026-10-02 (chicago-images rights-requests/ghm-george-glessner-2026-10.md). Read for what it shows; not shipped in the scene.
access_notes: Read from the owner's image store copy; the museum's original was not seen. The date is the blog's.
note: Spent by T-2478: the parkway trees and stone curb at the end of 18th Street, then the tracks on dark ground, then a row of white posts on the far side before the lake. No beach and no promenade shows between the tracks and the water.
what_it_supplies: The street's end against the right-of-way at 18th Street: curb, then cinder ground and tracks
That nothing like a beach or a public walk lay between the tracks and the water at 18th Street c. 1888
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority
